title: TokenFlow Divider: latency-first lane negotiation for prefill/decode
creator: Asha Varma
description:
Problem: tail latency for low-latency tenants is increasing when prefill-heavy batches are interleaved with long-decode requests on the same GPU. Current phase-based schedulers split prefill and decode but lack a lightweight arbitration mechanism that takes kernel cost, attention sparsity, and tenant latency preference into account.

Proposal: implement a TokenFlow Divider (TFD) that creates logically separate token "lanes" for requests at scheduling time and runs a lightweight priority negotiation to allocate micro-slices across lanes. Key features:
- Lane types: latency-sensitive (low headroom, hedged), throughput-optimized (bulk batches), and opportunistic background.
- Kernel hint propagation: callers include kernel-selection hints (fp16/4bit, matmul-fused) and attention-sparsity estimates; scheduler uses these for lane scoring and affinity.
- Proportional token budget: each tenant/lane is given a budget bucket; the TFD enforces soft proportional fairness with deficit smoothing to prevent starvation during bursty periods.
- Dynamic phase splitter: for long requests, the prefill stage can be split into sub-phases if KV cache size or attention-sparsity indicates diminishing returns, allowing earlier decode slices for latency lanes.
- Hedging and backoffs: latency lanes can initiate speculative decode hedges on a small percentage of tokens when predicted kernel slowdowns exceed a threshold.

Why different: unlike previous heavy-weight phase orchestrators this is intended to be a compact negotiation layer (sub-ms decision path) that augments kernel-aware schedulers with lane-level fairness and attention-aware splitting.

Goals and success metrics:
- Reduce 99th percentile latency for latency-tier customers by >= 25% under mixed workloads (measured on staged cluster).
- Keep aggregate throughput degradation <= 6% for mixed workloads vs baseline.
- No increase in OOMs or KV cache thrashing incidents in rollout cluster.

Constraints and trade-offs:
- Extra scheduling bookkeeping per request (small memory/CPU overhead). We limit metadata to a few bytes per request (lane id, deficit counter, kernel-hint flags).
- Potential throughput loss from splitting prefill early; mitigated via adaptive thresholding informed by attention-sparsity probe.
- Requires coordination with kernel-selection hints; if model onboarding lacks hints we fall back to conservative heuristics.

Rollout plan:
1) Simulation: run TFD in simulator with replay traces from prod (two-week mixed-tenant trace). (DONE)
2) Canary: enable TFD in canary cluster for non-critical tenants with telemetry. (IN PROGRESS)
3) Gradual ramp to latency-tier customers with opt-in flag, monitor tail latency and throughput.

Telemetry and dashboards:
- New Grafana panels: tfd.lane.allocations, tfd.deficit.distribution, tfd.kernel-hint-hit-rate, tfd.prefill-split-ratio.
- Alerts: tfd.99p-latency-regression > 20% for 10m, tfd.prefill-split-rate > 40% sustained.

Backward compatibility: when TFD is disabled, scheduler falls back to existing phase-arbiter. TFD is designed to be additive and configurable per deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private).
acceptance_criteria: Simulator shows >=20% p99 improvement for latency lanes on mixed trace
Canary run for 72h with no >10% throughput loss and no new OOMs
Kernel-hint integration validated for at least 3 model families (Llama2, Mistral, OPT)
Dashboard panels populated and alerts wired into oncall
comments: 2026-02-27 - Asha Varma: Initial design and simulation completed. Simulator used mixed-tenancy replay (2026-01 trace). Observed median latency improvement 12% and p99 28% for latency lanes. Throughput down 4%.

2026-03-02 - Miguel Santos: Implemented lightweight lane metadata (lane_id byte, deficit int16, kernel_hint bitmask). Microbenchmarks show scheduling decision adds ~120ns per request on canary hardware.

2026-03-05 - Priya Kulkarni (Reviewer): Concern about KV-cache fragmentation from aggressive prefill splitting. Suggested adding a split-stability window (default 200ms) to avoid oscillation. Added to design.
2026-03-07 - SRE Team (feedback): Recommend conservative defaults for hedging (1-2%) and automatic disable if GPU load > 90% to avoid cascading throttles.

2026-03-10 - Miguel Santos: Canary deployment started in cluster-canary-3 for tenant subset: latency-tier-alpha. Early telemetry: p99 reduced 22%, tail throughput stable. Observed one incident of increased small-kernel contention; investigating kernel hint decay heuristic.
2026-03-13 - Asha Varma: Updated split threshold logic to incorporate attention-sparsity probe output and kernel slow-start estimator. Pushed changes to branch feature/tfd-v2.
2026-03-14 - QA: End-to-end tests added for lane failover and hedging; found race where deficit counter reset could be lost on retry. Miguel preparing fix (PR link below).
implementation_notes: Core scheduler operator implemented in C++ hot path with a Go control-plane flag. Use atomics for deficit updates to avoid locks. Kernel-hint bools encoded in 8-bit mask to keep request meta thin. Added unit tests for split decision and fair-share bookkeeping.
